key_insight: Higher-order binary optimization (HUBO) can encode industrial logistics and scheduling more compactly than QUBO, reducing qubit demand but increasing circuit complexity.
engineering_relevance: For real-world routing and scheduling, HUBO may preserve constraints more faithfully and improve resource scaling, especially in hybrid quantum-classical workflows.
method: Formulated three representative logistics/manufacturing problems as HUBO models.
Compared HUBO encodings against corresponding QUBO formulations on qubit count and interaction order.
Benchmarked small routing instances with bias-field digitized counterdiabatic quantum optimization in simulation.
evidence_signal: The paper validates the formulations with classical solvers across multiple problem instances and performs a resource/scalability analysis using capacitated vehicle routing as a representative large-scale case.
watch_item: HUBO’s higher-order terms raise circuit depth, so current noisy hardware may not support practical execution without improved fidelity or early fault-tolerant devices.
paper_title: Quantum optimization beyond QUBO for industrial logistics and scheduling
